name: TheraNest vs Valant
title: TheraNest vs Valant: EHR Comparison for Mental Health Practices 2026
description: Compare TheraNest and Valant EHR platforms for behavioral health. See pricing, e-prescribing, features, and which is best for therapists vs psychiatrists.

summary.bottom_line: TheraNest is an affordable option for therapists and counselors with per-therapist pricing starting at $29/month. Valant is purpose-built for psychiatrists with native e-prescribing, EPCS, PDMP integration, and outcome measurement - making it the choice for prescribing clinicians and larger behavioral health organizations.

sections.heading: TheraNest vs Valant: Overview
sections.content: TheraNest and Valant serve different segments of behavioral health. TheraNest, now part of Ensora Health (formerly Therapy Brands), is designed for therapists, counselors, and social workers with affordable per-therapist pricing and over 200,000 providers. Valant was founded by a psychiatrist specifically for psychiatric practices and behavioral health organizations, with features like native e-prescribing, EPCS for controlled substances, PDMP integration, and built-in outcome measurement that prescribers need.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: TheraNest offers transparent, budget-friendly pricing: Essentials at $29/therapist/month, Advanced at $59/therapist/month with insurance billing, and Premier at $89/therapist/month with telehealth. Valant requires a custom quote with pricing typically $100-$300 per provider per month. For non-prescribing therapists, TheraNest is significantly more affordable. For psychiatrists needing e-prescribing, Valant's all-inclusive pricing may be more economical than seeking separate e-prescribing solutions.

sections.heading: Key Feature Differences
sections.content: The fundamental difference is e-prescribing: Valant has native e-prescribing with EPCS (controlled substances) and PDMP integration essential for psychiatrists, while TheraNest does not offer e-prescribing at all. Valant also has built-in outcome measurement tracking with PHQ-9, GAD-7, and other assessments. TheraNest has the advantage of mobile apps and Wiley Treatment Planner integration. For IOP/PHP programs, Valant offers specialized workflows.

sections.heading: Support & Implementation
sections.content: TheraNest offers a 21-day free trial allowing practices to test before committing, while Valant does not offer free trials but provides dedicated implementation support. Both are HIPAA compliant with BAA available. TheraNest's Ensora Health backing (KKR) provides stability, while Valant's psychiatrist-founded heritage ensures psychiatric-specific expertise.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: The choice is largely determined by whether you prescribe medications:

recommendations.when: You're a therapist, counselor, or social worker who doesn't prescribe and wants affordable, transparent pricing with good mobile apps
You're a psychiatrist, psychiatric NP, or prescriber needing native e-prescribing with EPCS and PDMP integration
You run an IOP/PHP program or need specialized psychiatric practice workflows with built-in outcome measurement
You use the Wiley Treatment Planner and want integrated treatment planning, or need mobile apps for on-the-go practice management

faqs.a: No, TheraNest does not offer e-prescribing capabilities. If you're a psychiatrist or prescribing clinician, Valant includes native e-prescribing with EPCS for controlled substances and PDMP integration.

faqs.q: Which is cheaper: TheraNest or Valant?
faqs.a: TheraNest is significantly cheaper for non-prescribing therapists, starting at $29/month. Valant typically costs $100-$300 per provider per month but includes e-prescribing and psychiatric-specific features that TheraNest lacks.

faqs.q: Is Valant better for psychiatrists than TheraNest?
faqs.a: Yes, Valant is purpose-built for psychiatrists with native e-prescribing, EPCS, PDMP integration, and psychiatric-specific templates. TheraNest is designed for therapists and counselors and does not offer prescribing capabilities.

TheraNest has basic outcome tracking, but Valant has more robust built-in outcome measurement with standardized assessments like PHQ-9 and GAD-7 integrated into clinical workflows for measurement-based care.
